subproblem.title: Regular level sets on a C¹ antilipschitz chart are covered by countably many C¹ bi-Lipschitz m-charts
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P of class C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} open with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω (some c > 0), h : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ of class C¹ and t ∈ ℝ. Then there are C¹ maps Ψ_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and open sets V_i ⊆ ℝ^m (i ∈ ℕ) such that each Ψ_i is Lipschitz on V_i and c_i-antilipschitz on V_i for some c_i > 0; for every w ∈ Ω with h(w) = t and Dh(w) ≠ 0 there are i and v ∈ V_i with Ψ_i(v) = Φ(w); and for every i and v ∈ V_i there is w ∈ Ω with h(w) = t, Ψ_i(v) = Φ(w) and DΨ_i(v)(ℝ^m) = DΦ(w)(ker Dh(w)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (h : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ) (t : ℝ), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → ∃ (Ψ : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl P) (V : ℕ → Set (Eucl m)), (∀ i, IsOpen (V i)) ∧ (∀ i, ContDiff ℝ 1 (Ψ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K (Ψ i) (V i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ V i, ∀ v' ∈ V i, c * ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖Ψ i v - Ψ i v'‖) ∧ (∀ w ∈ Ω, h w = t → fderiv ℝ h w ≠ 0 → ∃ i, ∃ v ∈ V i, Ψ i v = Φ w) ∧ ∀ i, ∀ v ∈ V i, ∃ w ∈ Ω, h w = t ∧ Ψ i v = Φ w ∧ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (Ψ i) v).toLinearMap = Submodule.map (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap (LinearMap.ker (fderiv ℝ h w).toLinearMap)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. B(v, r) is the open ball. Dψ(v) := fderiv ℝ ψ v. A map is c-antilipschitz on a set if c|v − v′| ≤ |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| there. This is the implicit-function part of Step 8 of the parent proof (slicing_im_slice_triple): 'by the implicit function theorem the set {w ∈ Ω_j : h_{jk}(w) = t, ∇h_{jk}(w) ≠ 0} is covered by countably many C¹ parametrizations ψ : V → ℝⁿ (V ⊆ ℝ^m open, Dψ injective, ψ bi-Lipschitz on V after shrinking), and Ψ := Φ_j∘ψ is C¹, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound'. Here it is made precise.
0. (Trivial case.) Let R := {w ∈ Ω : h(w) = t, Dh(w) ≠ 0}. If R = ∅, take V_i := ∅ and Ψ_i :≡ 0 for all i: every clause holds (vacuously, the antilipschitz clause with c_i := 1). Assume R ≠ ∅.
1. (Local graph parametrization at w₀ ∈ R.) Fix w₀ ∈ R and let ℓ := Dh(w₀) ≠ 0. Let a ∈ ℝ^{m+1} be its gradient (ℓ(u) = ⟨a, u⟩, a ≠ 0) and e := a/|a|², so ℓ(e) = 1. The kernel K₀ := ker ℓ = a^⊥ has dimension m. Fix a linear isometry ι₀ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} with range K₀ (from an orthonormal basis of K₀ indexed by Fin m; ι₀ = 0 if m = 0). Define the C¹ function H : ℝ^m × ℝ → ℝ, H(v, s) := h(w₀ + ι₀v + se). Then H(0, 0) = t, and the partial derivative of H in s at (0, 0) is s ↦ s·ℓ(e) = s, which is invertible. By the implicit function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.implicitFunction with implicitFunction_apply_self, eventually_apply_eq_iff_implicitFunction and contDiffAt_implicitFunction) there are a function g : ℝ^m → ℝ with g(0) = 0 that is C¹ at 0, and a neighbourhood N₀ of (0, 0) such that for (v, s) ∈ N₀: H(v, s) = t ⟺ s = g(v). Since g is C¹ at 0 it is C¹ on a neighbourhood of 0 (ContDiffAt.eventually); choose r₀ > 0 such that g is C¹ on B(0, 3r₀).
2. (Globalization.) Let χ : ℝ^m → [0, 1] be a C^∞ bump function with χ = 1 on B(0, r₀) and support in B(0, 2r₀) (ContDiffBump). Put g̃ := χ·g. Then g̃ is C¹ on ℝ^m: it is C¹ on B(0, 3r₀) as a product of C¹ functions, and it vanishes identically on the open set {|v| > 2r₀}; these two open sets cover ℝ^m. Moreover g̃ = g on B(0, r₀). Put ψ(v) := w₀ + ι₀v + g̃(v)e. Then ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} is C¹ and ψ(0) = w₀.
3. (ψ is 1-antilipschitz on ℝ^m.) ψ(v) − ψ(v′) = ι₀(v − v′) + (g̃(v) − g̃(v′))e with ι₀(v − v′) ∈ a^⊥ ⟂ e. By Pythagoras |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)|² = |v − v′|² + (g̃(v) − g̃(v′))²|e|² ≥ |v − v′|². Consequently Dψ(v) is injective with |Dψ(v)u| ≥ |u|, because |Dψ(v)u| = lim_{s→0} |ψ(v + su) − ψ(v)|/|s|.
4. (Chart domain.) Let A₀(v, s) := w₀ + ι₀v + se. Its linear part (v, s) ↦ ι₀v + se is a linear isomorphism ℝ^m × ℝ → ℝ^{m+1}: it is injective because ι₀ is injective with range a^⊥ and e ∉ a^⊥, and the dimensions agree. Hence A₀ is a homeomorphism. Choose r₁ > 0 and δ > 0 with B(0, r₁) × (−δ, δ) ⊆ N₀. Then choose r ∈ (0, min(r₀, r₁)] so small that for |v| < r: |g(v)| < δ (g is continuous at 0 and g(0) = 0); ψ(v) ∈ Ω (ψ is continuous, ψ(0) = w₀ ∈ Ω, Ω open); and Dh(ψ(v)) ≠ 0 (Dh is continuous and Dh(w₀) ≠ 0). Put V := B(0, r) and W := A₀(B(0, r) × (−δ, δ)), an open neighbourhood of w₀.
5. (The level set inside W is ψ(V).)
   - Let w ∈ W with h(w) = t. Write w = A₀(v, s) with |v| < r and |s| < δ. Then (v, s) ∈ N₀ and H(v, s) = h(w) = t, so s = g(v) = g̃(v) (as |v| < r ≤ r₀). Hence w = ψ(v) with v ∈ V.
   - Conversely, for v ∈ V we have (v, g(v)) ∈ B(0, r) × (−δ, δ) ⊆ N₀, so H(v, g(v)) = t. As ψ(v) = A₀(v, g(v)), this says h(ψ(v)) = t.
6. (The chart Ψ := Φ∘ψ on V.)
   - Ψ is C¹ as a composition of C¹ maps.
   - Ψ is Lipschitz on V: DΨ is continuous, hence bounded by some K on the compact convex set closedBall(0, r), so Ψ is K-Lipschitz on V by the mean value inequality (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le).
   - Ψ is c-antilipschitz on V: for v, v′ ∈ V, ψ(v), ψ(v′) ∈ Ω (step 4), so |Ψ(v) − Ψ(v′)| ≥ c|ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| ≥ c|v − v′| (step 3).
7. (Tangent spaces.) Let v ∈ V and w := ψ(v); then w ∈ Ω and h(w) = t (steps 4, 5), and Ψ(v) = Φ(w).
   - Since h∘ψ ≡ t on the open set V ∋ v, D(h∘ψ)(v) = Dh(w)∘Dψ(v) = 0, so range Dψ(v) ⊆ ker Dh(w).
   - range Dψ(v) has dimension m (step 3), and ker Dh(w) has dimension m since Dh(w) ≠ 0 (step 4). Hence range Dψ(v) = ker Dh(w).
   - By the chain rule DΨ(v) = DΦ(w)∘Dψ(v), so range DΨ(v) = DΦ(w)(range Dψ(v)) = DΦ(w)(ker Dh(w)).
8. (Countably many charts.) Steps 1–7 give, for each w₀ ∈ R, a triple (Ψ_{w₀}, V_{w₀}, W_{w₀}) with W_{w₀} an open neighbourhood of w₀. Every w ∈ W_{w₀} with h(w) = t is ψ_{w₀}(v) for some v ∈ V_{w₀}, so Φ(w) = Ψ_{w₀}(v). Since ℝ^{m+1} is second countable, the family {W_{w₀} : w₀ ∈ R} has a countable subfamily with the same union (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). That union contains R. Enumerate the countable subfamily, nonempty since R ≠ ∅, as w_i (i ∈ ℕ, repetitions allowed), and set Ψ_i := Ψ_{w_i}, V_i := V_{w_i}.
9. (Verification.)
   - Each V_i is open; each Ψ_i is C¹, Lipschitz on V_i and c-antilipschitz on V_i (step 6).
   - If w ∈ Ω, h(w) = t and Dh(w) ≠ 0, then w ∈ R lies in some W_{w_i}, so Φ(w) = Ψ_i(v) for some v ∈ V_i (step 8).
   - For v ∈ V_i, w := ψ_{w_i}(v) satisfies w ∈ Ω, h(w) = t, Ψ_i(v) = Φ(w) and range DΨ_i(v) = DΦ(w)(ker Dh(w)) (step 7).
   For m = 0 every step holds verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, ι₀ = 0, V = ℝ⁰, ψ ≡ w₀ and Ψ ≡ Φ(w₀). Then range DΨ = {0} = DΦ(w₀)(ker Dh(w₀)), because Dh(w₀) ≠ 0 is injective on ℝ¹, and the regular points of the level set are isolated. ∎
proof_key_steps: At a regular point w₀ of the level set {h = t} ∩ Ω, the implicit function theorem for H(v, s) = h(w₀ + ι₀v + se), with ι₀ an isometry onto ker Dh(w₀) and Dh(w₀)e = 1, gives a C¹ graph function g.
Globalize g with a bump function. ψ(v) = w₀ + ι₀v + g̃(v)e is C¹ on ℝ^m and 1-antilipschitz by Pythagoras.
Shrink to a ball V so that ψ(V) ⊆ Ω, Dh ≠ 0 on ψ(V), and the level set inside an open W ∋ w₀ is exactly ψ(V).
Ψ := Φ∘ψ is C¹, Lipschitz on V (mean value inequality) and c-antilipschitz on V, with range DΨ(v) = DΦ(ψ v)(ker Dh(ψ v)) by dimension count.
A countable subcover of the open sets W (second countability) gives the charts Ψ_i, V_i.

audit.reason: The proof establishes the exact global-C¹ chart contract: implicit graphs are globalized with a bump, orthogonality supplies the lower Lipschitz bound, compact derivative bounds supply the upper bound, and the chain rule and dimension count identify tangent ranges. Second countability gives the required enumeration. Empty regular sets and m = 0 are covered.
